text.p: IOC President Juan Antonio Samaranch has praised the Barcelona Summer Games as the best of all time and said the Atlanta Olympics were marred by a long list of shortcomings.

In an interview with the Frankfurt Allgemeine Zeitung published on Thursday, Samaranch said he did not proclaim the Atlanta Games with the usual post-Olympic superlative because of the multitude of problems ranging from transport bottlenecks to technology failures.
"I was right by not talking of the 'best games ever'," Samaranch told the newspaper in an interview in Cancun, Mexico. "Imagine would the world would have said if I had called these the best games."

He said long waits for Olympic participants in receiving their accreditation, poorly trained drivers who got lost on the way to events, technology problems and the failure to coordinate security were all deficiencies in Atlanta.

"I wouldn't say the Americans (were angry), rather the people in Atlanta," Samarach said of his famous snub. "I believe the media in America were in agreement with my judgement of the games. They were extraordinary but not the best."

Samarach said that he had also withheld the superlative "best Games ever" after the Sarajevo winter Olympics in 1984, in Albertville in 1992 and "I believe also in Los Angeles in 1984. I only say that when is true. No one can dispute that Lillehammer were the best winter Games and Barcelona the best summer Games."
But Samaranch told the newspaper: "Atlanta is in the past. The past is the past. It teaches you some lessons but that is all."
Samaranch said that Atlanta was nevertheless a success.

"The start in Atlanta wasn't exactly what it should be, but in the end with had quite extraordinary games," he said. "There was record attendance, the competitions were very good and last but not least -- the television ratings were excellent.
"Many say now that, well, NBC was rather chauvinistic. But NBC was only making its programme for the United States. It was completely different from what people in Germany were seeing."
